title: CLO 2026.0 - Adhesion
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! Attach panels to designated positions through various methods such as padding, brushes, or quick bonding to achieve dynamic simulation of accessory panels like pockets or labels, making your workflow faster and smoother!
transcript:
Hello everyone, we are very happy to be able to launch a new integrated function in the CLO 2026.0 update.  
Previously, you had to use sewing lines or fake sewing to fix pockets and decals.  
Now, using the integrated tool, you can apply glue to the entire board or a specific area to make the two boards perfectly integrated.  
The integrated function is designed to support a seamless structure.  
Next, let's take a look at how these functions work in the actual workflow.  

The first function I will demonstrate is the fill-in-integration tool.  
Select the fill-in-integration tool from the 2D toolbar.  
The tool can automatically identify the border or internal shape of the board and quickly define the integrated area.  
First, you need to ensure that the internal shape on the basic board is the same as that of the integrated purple board.  
Then, place the purple board accurately on the upper part of the basic board.  
Click on the purple board.  
After clicking on the purple board, the board will be displayed in orange color.  
This shows that the integrated connection has been established.  
After the integration, you can move the board at will.  
The integrated state will remain unchanged.  
This tool works the same way in the 3D window.  
Place the purple board close to the front or back of the basic board.  
At this time, the purple board in the 2D window does not need to overlap with the basic board.  
Use the fill-in-integration tool to click on the purple board to set the integration.  
When the tool is activated, you will see the fill-in-integration option window in the upper right corner of the 3D window.  
If you change the mode to subtract and click on the integrated board, the integration will be removed.  

For this kind of gray bar, we can also use the quick integration tool.  
It allows you to paste a board into the exact position you want.  
Select the quick integration tool in the 2D toolbar.  
Click on the board you want to integrate.  
A gray bar with the outline of a board will move along your mouse cursor.  
Use this guide to determine the integration position on the basic board and then click again.  
The biggest advantage of the quick integration tool is that you don't have to manually overlap the board in the 2D window in advance.  
The gray bar can help you specify the entire integration area immediately.  

Next, I will explain how to cancel the quick integration.  
You need to switch to the fill-in-integration tool first.  
In the mode of the fill-in-integration window, select subtract.  
Click on the integrated board to cancel.  
After opening the simulation, you can see that the board has been removed from the large board.  
Use the quick integration tool to re-integrate this board.  

Finally, let's take a look at the pen and brush integration tool.  
Replace the purple board onto the basic board.  
In the 2D toolbar, click and hold the integration tool for 2 seconds.  
Then select the pen and brush integration from the purple menu.  
Unlike the pen and brush integration for the entire board or the internal shape integration,  
using the pen and brush integration can freely specify the integration area on the board.  
When the two boards are re-integrated,  
you only need to drag the area you want to re-integrate to apply.  
The orange color will appear on the screen.  
When you run the simulation, you will see the purple board  
perfectly along the area of the orange color,  
re-integrated on the basic board.  

Let's take a look at the setting of the pen and brush integration in the upper right corner.  
There are two types.  
The outer is the type just displayed.  
It is the reverse of the glue applied to the purple board,  
making it re-integrated to the outer of the basic board.  
This type is used in most cases.  
On the integration of the board to the board,  
the inner side is the surface of the glue applied to the basic board,  
making it re-integrated to the inner side of the purple board.  
In short, although the position of the glue is different,  
the result is the same.  
The two boards are firmly re-integrated into one whole.  

Change between increase or decrease mode  
to create a new re-integration area or remove some existing areas.  
Adjust the pen and brush size to adapt to your board.  
You can drag and slide or enter a specific value  
to apply fine details or enlarge the area.  

According to your work process,  
the 2D window or 3D window  
may be different in different cases.  
The 2D window is most suitable for  
completely matching the shape of the two boards,  
or when the structure of the layer is simple,  
it will be faster and more convenient to use.  
The 3D window is most suitable for  
different shapes of boards,  
or when you need to place the board accurately  
and use it in the complex curved structure of the simulation.  
Please consider the shape and structure of your board  
to choose the window that is most suitable for the situation.  

This function is widely used not only for clothing,  
but also for painting.  
It is also used for other types of products,  
such as shoes, hats, etc.  
Try to use the integrated function  
to paste the sticker label or the wireless pocket.  
You will be able to create the layer effect of the pen  
more quickly and more easily.  

We hope you can explore in various design projects  
and enjoy the fun of using these new tools.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Adhesion
chunks.content: ## Introduction to CLO 2026.0 Adhesion Integrated Function This section introduces the new integrated adhesion function in CLO 2026.0, designed to replace previous methods such as sewing lines or fake sewing for fixing pockets and decals. The function allows users to apply glue either to an entire board or a specific area, enabling seamless integration of two boards for a smooth, unified structure. --- ## Fill-In Integration Tool: Automatic Area Detection and Integration This section explains the fill-in integration tool, which automatically detects board borders or internal shapes to define integration areas quickly. - **Workflow:** - Select the fill-in integration tool from the 2D toolbar. - Ensure the internal shape of the basic board matches the purple integrated board. - Accurately place the purple board on top of the basic board. - Click on the purple board; it will highlight in orange, indicating integration. - After integration, the board can be freely moved while maintaining the integrated state. - **3D Window Usage:** - Place the purple board near the front or back of the basic board without requiring overlap in 2D. - Click the purple board with the fill-in integration tool to set integration. - The fill-in integration options appear in the upper right corner of the 3D window. - Switching the mode to “subtract” and clicking the integrated board removes the integration. --- ## Quick Integration Tool: Precise Positioning Without Manual Overlap This section covers the quick integration tool, which helps position a board exactly where desired without manual overlap. - **Usage:** - Select the quick integration tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click the board to integrate; a gray bar outlining the board follows the cursor. - Move the gray bar to the desired integration position on the basic board and click to integrate. - **Advantages:** - Eliminates the need to manually overlap boards in the 2D window. - Provides an immediate visual guide for integration area placement. - **Cancelling Quick Integration:** - Switch to the fill-in integration tool. - Set the mode to “subtract” in the fill-in integration window. - Click the integrated board to cancel integration. - The board will be removed from the large board after simulation. - Quick integration can be reapplied as needed. --- ## Pen and Brush Integration Tool: Custom Area Adhesion This section describes the pen and brush integration tool, which allows freehand specification of integration areas on boards. - **Activation:** - Place the purple board on the basic board. - In the 2D toolbar, click and hold the integration tool for 2 seconds. - Select pen and brush integration from the pop-up menu. - **Functionality:** - Unlike full-board or internal shape integration, this tool lets users drag over specific areas to apply or reapply integration. - Selected areas highlight in orange. - Upon simulation, the purple board adheres perfectly along the orange-highlighted areas.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Adhesion
chunks.content: - **Activation:** - Place the purple board on the basic board. - In the 2D toolbar, click and hold the integration tool for 2 seconds. - Select pen and brush integration from the pop-up menu. - **Functionality:** - Unlike full-board or internal shape integration, this tool lets users drag over specific areas to apply or reapply integration. - Selected areas highlight in orange. - Upon simulation, the purple board adheres perfectly along the orange-highlighted areas. - **Settings:** - Two integration types are available: - **Outer:** Applies glue to the purple board, integrating it to the outer side of the basic board (most common). - **Inner:** Applies glue to the basic board, integrating it to the inner side of the purple board. - Both achieve firm adhesion; the difference lies in glue placement. - **Mode and Size Adjustments:** - Switch between increase (add) and decrease (remove) modes to modify integration areas. - Adjust brush size by dragging the slider or entering numeric values for fine detail or larger areas. --- ## Choosing Between 2D and 3D Windows for Integration This section advises on selecting the appropriate workspace window based on board shape and complexity. - **2D Window:** - Best for completely matching shapes of two boards. - More convenient and faster when layer structures are simple. - **3D Window:** - Ideal for boards with different shapes or complex curved structures. - Allows precise placement of boards in simulation. Users should evaluate the shape and structure of their boards to decide which window suits their integration tasks best. --- ## Applications and Use Cases of Adhesion Integration This section highlights the broad applicability of the new adhesion function beyond apparel design. - Commonly used for: - Clothing details like pockets and decals. - Painting applications. - Other product types, including shoes and hats. - Practical tips: - Use the integrated function to attach sticker labels or wireless pockets. - Enables faster and easier creation of layered effects using the pen tool. --- ## Summary CLO 2026.0’s adhesion integration tools—fill-in integration, quick integration, and pen and brush integration—provide versatile methods for seamlessly combining boards. These tools support precise, flexible, and efficient workflows in both 2D and 3D environments, suitable for a variety of product designs and structures.
